newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end sharply lower on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end sharply lower on fund selling.

text.p: Chilean shares skidded to close sharply weaker on strong selling by a foreign fund with the bolsa depressed by the prospect of large-scale sales by a second international fund this year, said traders.
The bolsa is expected to open weaker on Monday with investors fearing a repeat of the liquidation by the GT Chile Growth Fund earlier this year, which dragged down the market for months.
"Monday looks black. The market is taking the sales very badly," said one trader. The 40-share IPSA index ended down 1.1 percent at 95.29 points.
The general IGPA index shed 0.8 percent to 5,204.97 points. Volume was a moderate 10 billion pesos.
Traders reported selective selling by the $400 million Genesis Chile Fund, which is run by fund manager Intergenesis.
Fund officials were not available for comment.
The traders did not know the reason for the sales.
The strongest decliners included stocks like bottler Andina in which the fund has heavy investments.
The Genesis fund has 17 percent of its portfolio invested in Andina, one of Chile's largest soft drinks bottlers.
Andina was also hurt by news CS First Boston has cut its recommendation for the stock to hold from buy.
Other losers included telecoms company Telex, down 3.52 percent at 1,180 pesos and steel producer Cap, which shed 3.35 percent to 1,010 pesos.

Winners included copper company Mantos, up 1.49 percent at 680 pesos, copper products maker Madeco, up 0.94 percent at 970 pesos and salmon producer Mainstream which rose 0.76 percent at 33.25 pesos. -- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 ext-212
